newsitem.title: USA: Nautica's solid profits fail to boost stock.
newsitem.headline: Nautica's solid profits fail to boost stock.

text.p: Shares of Nautica Enterprises Inc dropped on Friday despite solid earnings gains as investors fear apparel stocks may be ripe for a drop.
"Christmas sales may have been a bit weaker than expected, but the stock (Nautica) is reacting to interest rate fears," said Elizabeth Vandeventer, an analyst with S&P Equity Group.
"Whenever there is speculation about interest rates, investors pull their money out of apparel stocks, which are very risky, and put them into more stable stocks," Vandeventer said.
Shares of the men's sportswear company dropped 2-1/8 to 24-7/8.
This dip sparked a selloff in Tommy Hilfiger Corp, a men's apparel company with similar style and pricing, analysts said. Tommy Hilfiger dropped 1-1/2 to 44-1/2.
Earlier on Friday, Nautica posted third quarter earnings of $0.37 a share on net sales of $116.6 million, up from earnings of $0.28 or $90.8 million a year ago.
Both Nautica and Tommy Hilfiger have seen strong sales and growing brand recognition, as consumers shift toward more casual clothing.
Tommy Hilfiger "has been doing wonderfully," said Lee Backus, an analyst with Buckingham Research Group.
But analysts said consumer spending on apparel is expected to slow. Apparel stocks could continue to face pressure until interest rates ease.

Interest rate fears often depress cyclical stocks, such as the apparel sector. When rates jump, consumers have less discretionary income and often spend less on apparel and luxury goods, analysts said.
